diagnosis: The image shows a single exact bottleneck pair, with both points having one contact and the other 91 points having none at the $10^{-9}$ threshold, so the code is not a jammed, rigid local optimum. However, roughly 500 pairs lie within a few $10^{-6}$ of the maximum, creating an extremely ill-conditioned near-contact plateau in which moving the bottleneck pair is immediately obstructed by other pairs. This explains why micro-LP, pair repulsion, and small isotropic basin hops from the record produce only $10^{-8}$--$10^{-5}$ gains and repeatedly return to essentially the same configuration. The missing structural property is a large, exactly equalized, stress-balanced contact set—ideally hundreds of tied pairs distributed across most points—that makes every feasible first-order motion increase some contact. Real progress requires either precisely tying that near-contact cloud in the present basin or deliberately changing which pairs form the contact graph.

Its contact structure is also badly unbalanced—most points have 14–33 contacts, but one point is a rattler with zero contacts, meaning one point occupies an oversized cavity while the remaining 92 are overloaded. The missing structural property is therefore balanced, isotropic rigidity: every point should be active, degrees and row-wise maxima should be much more homogeneous, and \(X^{T}X\) should be close to \((93/13)I\), with no hub points or wasted rattler. Random shakes, single-point deletions, and ordinary re-polishing keep returning to this same contact topology, so improvement requires explicitly changing the contact graph or imposing different global structure.
